references.text: The regulation concerning the sin offering with a male goat for a leader who has sinned. This illustrates the general law followed in Numbers 7:46.
Moses commands the people to take a male goat as a sin offering, demonstrating the same sacrificial practice.
The same offering was given by the tribal leader on the first day of consecration, showing the recurring pattern.
An identical sin offering from another tribal leader's gift, confirming the common sacrificial arrangement.
The same wording is used for the sin offering of another leader, demonstrating unified practice.
A male goat for a sin offering is mentioned as part of the community's offering for unintentional sins.
A male goat for a sin offering to the Lord shall be sacrificed at the new moon, showing continued use of this offering.
King Hezekiah commanded that male goats be offered as sin offerings for all Israel.
At the temple dedication after the exile, male goats were sacrificed as sin offerings for all Israel.
